## TL;DR

Completed the requested Stories page and story detail QA pass against the auth-less dev server using headless Playwright at 1280×900 and 375×812. The populated list, mobile layout, detail tabs, linked tasks, completed filter, and sort menu worked in the observed run. Existing component tests cover the disabled and empty states. I found no reproducible product defect, so no UI code change was needed. The QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-stories-detail.md`.

## Work and rationale

I read the task specification, inspected the Stories view and its list/detail tests, then launched `just serve-noauth 7272` from a detached scratch worktree rooted at the assigned branch tip. That follows the repository's isolation guidance: the server process built and served a scratch checkout, rather than watching the active task checkout or the main checkout. Playwright WebKit ran headlessly; I did not open a visible browser or use the user's Chrome profile.

I used a desktop viewport of 1280×900 and a phone viewport of 375×812. On the populated live repository, the Stories page rendered 12 cards. At both widths, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` equaled the viewport width, so there was no page-level horizontal overflow. At 375px, the story detail drawer also fit: the drawer was 375px wide and its internal scroll width was 374px. I opened the story detail and checked that Story, PM, Tasks, and Details tabs appeared and were selectable. The Tasks tab displayed linked task numbers and statuses. The live task rows opened a task drawer, and Escape closed the active drawer.

I toggled Hide Completed Stories and observed its checkbox state change. I opened the sort menu, confirmed all three options (Most recently updated, Task number newest, Task number oldest), selected the oldest task-number ordering, and observed the card order and selected label update. No page errors were recorded during the interaction run. The controlled disabled/no-stories/all-complete states cannot be produced naturally from the current live repository payload without changing server data; the existing StoriesView component tests set those store fixtures directly and assert the corresponding states. I documented the division between live browser checks and fixture-backed test coverage in the QA record.

No reproducible bug emerged from the pass, so I left the UI implementation unchanged instead of adding a speculative fix. The targeted `stories-view.test.ts` and `story-panel.test.ts` run passed all 61 tests, including the disabled and empty-state fixture assertions. The required changed-path RepoOS check passed; its configured docs-only policy skipped the full build, broad tests, and UI smoke stages. The QA record is the durable artifact requested by the task. Scratch screenshots and build output stay under the ignored `.repoos/` directory and are not included in the deliverable.

## Approaches tried

I first waited for `networkidle`; that navigation did not settle because RepoOS maintains live polling. I changed the browser flow to wait for `domcontentloaded` and then for page-specific selectors such as `.story-card` and `.drawer`. This made navigation deterministic without disabling application behavior. I also used actual repository stories and tasks for populated states, then relied on the existing component tests for the controlled empty and disabled fixtures.

## Challenges and blockers

The main testing constraint was the continuously active network connection, which makes `networkidle` an unsuitable readiness condition for this app. One early interaction script also tried to click the page filter while a linked task drawer was still open; the dialog correctly intercepted the click. I reset the flow and verified drawer dismissal before testing the filter. These were test-script sequencing issues, not application defects. No task-level blocker remains.

## Key learnings

For RepoOS browser checks, use DOM readiness plus explicit view selectors instead of `networkidle`. Keep live-data checks separate from state-fixture component tests when server state should remain untouched. On this pass, viewport measurements, successful interactions, and the existing fixture assertions together provide coverage for the requested page states without inventing repository data or making unnecessary implementation changes.
